dataset.name: Depth-resolved soil data from DOE-LM Riverton Wyoming site, April-September 2017
description: Averaged (from 3 to 5 replicates) and QA/QC:d data for soil cores taken roughly every month in the period April 5 to September 13 in 2017 at a location close to DOE Legacy Management well 855 at the Riverton, Wyoming floodplain site. The groundwater at this site exhibits persistent U, Mo, and sulfate plumes and is one of the field sites in focus for the SLAC Groundwater Quality SFA program. Cores were separated into 5-20 cm segments based on soil horizonation and each segment was subsampled for microbial analyses (data available at the NCBI Single Read Archive (SRA) Database, https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/sra/, BioProject ID# PRJNA626616) in addition to the soil analyses included in this dataset. The soil analyses dataset includes aerobic and anaerobic respiration rate estimates (MicroResp method), water content estimates (on collected samples, not in situ), total C, N, S, Ca, K, Mg, Na, Fe, As, Mo, U, and organic-C concentrations, water extractable concentrations of the same elements, and HCl-extractable Fe(II) concentrations.

There are four files included in this data package: metadataFile.csv, avgDataFile.csv, methodFile.csv, and RVT2017soilData.xlsx. The excel file contains the same information as the individual csv-files (in separate tabs).

measurementTechnique: Total C and N: 20-40 mg of pulverized dry sediment, analyzed on a Carlo Erba NA1500 elemental analyzer
HCl-extractable Fe(II): 1:10 sediment:0.5 M HCl extraction, 2 hr shake, centrifuge 4000 rpm, filtration (0.22 um), ferrozine colorimetric analysis

Carbonate-C: Dropwise addition of 1 M HCl to soil suspension until effervescence ceases, decanting and drying @ 30 °C until completely dry (5-7 days). 20-40 mg of pulverized dry sediment, analyzed on a Carlo Erba NA1500 elemental analyzer.
Water-extractable elements: 1:10 sediment:milliQ extraction, 2 hr shake, centrifuge 4000 rpm, filtration (0.22 um)
Total element concentrations (except C and N): 1-3 g of pulverized sediment analyzed by X-ray Fluorescence Spectroscopy on an Spectro Xepos HE
ICP-MS analyses of water extracts (trace elements): inductively coupled plasma mass spectroscopy (Thermo XSeries II)
ICP-OES analyses of water extracts (Fe, Ca, S, K, Na, Mg): inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES, iCAP6000, Thermo Scientific, Cambridge, UK)

MicroResp measurements of aerobic and anaerobic respiration: colorimetric assay of CO2 produced from field moist sediment incubated in MicroResp system for 18 hrs at current soil temperature (determined by permanently installed TDR moisture sensors at ~1 m depth), either in air (aerobic) or 95%N2/5% H2 atmosphere (anaerobic).
MicroResp procedure modified from: Campbell, C.D., Chapman, S.J., Cameron, C.M., Davidson, M.S., and Potts, J.M. 2003. A rapid microtiter plate method to measure carbon dioxide evolved from carbon amendments so as to determine the physiological profiles of soil microbial communities by using whole soil. Applied & Environmental Microbiology, 69(6), 3593-3599
Gravimetric determination of soil moisture content: Weighing of samples before and after drying at 105°C for a minimum of 12 hours.
